Objectives

❖To build Dynamic Portfolio Rebalancing using Reinforcement Learning - an intelligent web-based portfolio management platform integrating Reinforcement Learning (PPO) and the classical Merton model for dynamic asset allocation.
❖To train a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent on a 13-feature market state space with a Softmax-constrained 3-asset action space (NIFTY 50, NASDAQ-100, Cash).
❖To implement a multi-objective reward function combining portfolio return, Sharpe ratio, drawdown penalty, and transaction cost efficiency for robust, risk-aware learning.
❖To provide an interactive web dashboard with live market charts, volatility regime indicators, and real-time KPI cards for side-by-side strategy comparison.
❖To enable user-configurable parameter tuning of risk aversion γ, transaction cost rate, and risk-free rate with instant re-evaluation and strategy comparison.

Deep Reinforcement Learning for Portfolio Optimisation
Jiang et al., 2017, NIPS Workshop on ML for Finance
CNN + RNN policy network with continuous portfolio rebalancing
First to demonstrate RL outperforming buy-and-hold on equity data end-to-end.
Ignores transaction costs; assumes zero market impact.
PPO, SAC and DDPG for Financial Portfolio Management
Zhang & Liu, 2022, IEEE Trans. Neural Networks
Benchmark of PPO, SAC, DDPG on S&P 500 with Sharpe-based rewards
Reveals PPO stability advantage over off-policy methods in non-stationary markets.
Uses only US equities; NIFTY+NASDAQ cross-market scope unexplored.
Dynamic Portfolio Rebalancing through Reinforcement Learning
Yang, Lim, Cao & Quek, 2021, Springer (Published online 27 Dec 2021)
RL-based dynamic rebalancing with transaction cost-aware reward; benchmarked against static strategies
Demonstrates adaptive rebalancing frequency; significantly reduces unnecessary trades.
Model evaluated only on select US equities; emerging market generalization not tested.
Option Pricing When Underlying Stock Returns Are Discontinuous
Robert C. Merton, 1976, Journal of Financial Economics
Jump-diffusion stochastic process model for asset return dynamics
Extends Black-Scholes to handle sudden price jumps; foundational model for financial engineering.
Assumes known jump intensity and size distribution; hard to calibrate on real-time data.

Merton's Intertemporal CAPM and the Cross-Section of Returns
Campbell & Vuolteenaho, 2004, American Economic Review
HJB continuous-time solution; closed-form Merton optimal portfolio weights with CRRA utility
Tractable closed-form weights serve as the interpretable classical benchmark for RL comparison.
Assumes constant μ and σ; ignores volatility regime changes and transaction costs.
Reward Shaping for Risk-Adjusted Portfolio Optimisation
Wang et al., 2023, Journal of Financial Data Science
Multi-objective PPO reward: return + α·Sharpe − λ₁·Drawdown − λ₂·Turnover
Reward shaping significantly reduces max drawdown without sacrificing annual returns.
Hyperparameters (α, λ₁, λ₂) require extensive grid search.
Transaction Cost-Aware Portfolio Rebalancing via RL
Park & Kim, 2023, Quantitative Finance
PPO with proportional transaction cost embedded in environment step
RL adapts rebalancing frequency dynamically to minimise total transaction drag.
Performance degrades under high-frequency microstructure noise.
Volatility Regime Detection with HMMs for Asset Allocation
Nystrup et al., 2020, European Journal of Operational Research
HMM regime switching + Markowitz optimisation per detected regime
Regime-conditioned allocation significantly reduces drawdowns during crises.
Online HMM updating introduces parameter instability.

texts.text: Problem Identification
❖Existing portfolio systems rely on static rule-based models such as Merton that assume constant market parameters, failing to adapt to volatile or crisis regimes.
❖Classical strategies have no mechanism to learn from market experience - they recompute weights with fixed formulae regardless of evolving market conditions.
❖Most research tools are Python scripts inaccessible to non-technical investors; there is no interactive interface for parameter exploration or real-time strategy comparison.
❖There is no unified platform for side-by-side comparison of AI-driven (RL) and classical portfolio strategies with live market data and performance metrics.
❖Current RL systems lack explainability and investor trust - investors cannot understand why the AI chose a specific allocation, reducing real-world adoption.
Proposed System & Modules
Platform Type: Full-stack, intelligent portfolio management platform named Dynamic Portfolio Rebalancing using Reinforcement Learning.
Core Function: Enables investors to simulate, backtest, and visualise AI-driven Reinforcement Learning (PPO) strategies versus the classical Merton model.
Market Data Used: Live NIFTY 50 & NASDAQ-100 market data.
Primary Objective: Bridges the gap between academic research and practical finance.
Platform Features: Interactive web dashboard, secure authentication, live data integration, and configurable strategy parameters.
PROJECT MODULES
•  Module 1 : Interactive Web Dashboard
•  Module 2 : User Login & Authentication
•  Module 3 : Live Market Data Integration
•  Module 4 : RL Working Process
•  Module 5 : Portfolio Tracker
•  Module 6 : Strategy Parameter Tuning Panel
Module 1 : Interactive Web Dashboard
The Interactive Web Dashboard is the public-facing entry point of Dynamic Portfolio Rebalancing using Reinforcement Learning.

It replaces all static .png charts with a fully live, browser-based analytical environment where users can explore NIFTY 50 and NASDAQ-100 market data, monitor volatility conditions, and compare RL vs Merton portfolio performance in real time without touching any Python code.
Key Features:
•  Live Plotly charts display NIFTY 50 & NASDAQ-100 price history with EMA 20 and EMA 60 trend overlays; all charts are zoomable, pannable, and hoverable.
•  Volatility Regime Badge dynamically updates to 'Normal' or '⚠ HIGH STRESS' based on whether the 20-day volatility exceeds the 60-day rolling average for either index.
•  KPI metric cards display live values for Sharpe Ratio, Maximum Drawdown, and Annualised Return for both RL and Merton strategies — updated on every data refresh.
•  Underwater Drawdown Chart visualises capital loss from peak over time, allowing investors to compare crisis resilience of the RL agent vs. the classical Merton model.
⚙ Tech Stack:  Streamlit / Flask  |  Plotly (interactive charts)  |  yfinance (live data feed)  |  Pandas
Module 2 : User Login & Authentication
The User Login & Authentication module provides a secure identity layer that gates access to personalised portfolio features.
Only authenticated users can access the Portfolio Tracker and Parameter Tuning Panel.
The system uses industry-standard cryptographic practices to ensure that user credentials and session data are protected at all times.
Key Features:
•  Registration flow collects username, email, and password; passwords are hashed using bcrypt with adaptive salt rounds before being stored in the database.
•  Login flow verifies the submitted password against the stored bcrypt hash; on success, a signed JSON Web Token (JWT) is issued with a configurable expiry window.
•  All protected API routes validate the JWT on every request; expired or tampered tokens are rejected with a 401 Unauthorized response, forcing re-authentication.
•  Session management routes the authenticated user to their dedicated Portfolio Tracker workspace, resolving their account record and personal NAV history from the database.
⚙ Tech Stack:  Flask / FastAPI (backend)  |  bcrypt (password hashing)  |  JWT (session tokens)  |  SQLite / PostgreSQL
Module 3 : Live Market Data Integration
The Live Market Data Integration module replaces the static Excel input file with a fully automated, real-time data pipeline.

On every session or scheduled refresh, the system fetches the latest daily closing prices for NIFTY 50 and NASDAQ-100, computes all 13 RL state features in-memory, and passes the updated state vector directly to the PPO agent - eliminating any manual data collection or Excel maintenance.
Key Features:
•  yfinance API pulls daily OHLCV data for ^NSEI (NIFTY 50) and ^NDX (NASDAQ-100); historical data from a configurable lookback window (default: 2 years) is downloaded automatically.
•  All 13 RL state features are computed in-memory using Pandas: log returns, 20-day & 60-day rolling volatility, drawdown from running max, rolling Sharpe ratio, and volatility regime flag.
•  The live RL state vector is fed to the trained PPO model, which outputs 'Today’s Recommended Allocation' (% NASDAQ, % NIFTY, % Cash) displayed on the dashboard.
•  A data quality validation step detects gaps or NaN values in the live feed and applies forward-fill imputation to ensure continuous, uninterrupted model inference.
⚙ Tech Stack:  yfinance (market data API)  |  Pandas (feature engineering)  |  NumPy  |  APScheduler (scheduled refresh)
Module 4 : RL Working Process
The RL Working Process module is the core intelligence engine of Dynamic Portfolio Rebalancing using Reinforcement Learning
A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent is trained on historical NIFTY 50 & NASDAQ-100 data using a custom Gymnasium environment.

The agent learns to dynamically allocate portfolio weights across three assets by maximising a multi-objective reward that balances return, risk-adjusted performance, downside protection, and transaction cost efficiency.
Key Features:
•  State Space (13 features): Log Returns, Vol20, Vol60, Drawdown, Volatility Regime, Rolling 60-day Return, and Rolling Sharpe Ratio - computed separately for both NIFTY and NASDAQ.
•  Action Space: 3 raw logits from the PPO MLP [256 -128 - 64] pass through Softmax to produce non-negative portfolio weights summing to 1: (w_NASDAQ, w_NIFTY, w_Cash).
•  Multi-objective Reward:  r_portfolio + α·Sharpe − λ₁·|Drawdown| − λ₂·Turnover (α=0.5, λ₁=2.0, λ₂=0.1); transaction cost of 0.1% deducted on every rebalancing step.
•  Training: 100,000 PPO timesteps with learning rate 3×10⁻⁴, n_steps=2048, batch_size=64, γ=0.99; model weights saved and loaded for live inference without retraining.
⚙ Tech Stack:  Stable-Baselines3 (PPO)  |  Gymnasium (custom PortfolioEnv)  |  PyTorch (neural network backend)
Module 5 : Portfolio Tracker
The Portfolio Tracker is the personalised workspace available to authenticated users.
It provides a real-time view of the user’s portfolio performance, current asset allocation, and historical NAV growth driven by the active strategy (PPO RL Agent or Merton Benchmark).
The tracker updates automatically after every market data refresh and rebalancing event, giving the investor a clear, data-driven picture of their financial position.
Key Features:
•  Summary bar displays Total Portfolio NAV (₹), Unrealised Daily P&L (₹ and %), Available Cash Balance, and Active Strategy Badge (PPO AI Agent or Merton Benchmark).
•  Asset Allocation Donut Chart renders the current portfolio split across NASDAQ, NIFTY, and Cash as percentages, redrawn after every rebalancing event.
•  Cumulative NAV Line Chart plots portfolio growth from inception, with an optional overlay comparing the simultaneously-running alternative strategy (RL vs Merton).
•  Holdings Table provides an itemised breakdown for each asset: current weight (%), market value (₹), daily return (%), and total contribution to portfolio P&L.
⚙ Tech Stack:  Plotly (donut chart, NAV curve)  |  Pandas (NAV engine, P&L computation)  |  SQLite (trade ledger)
Module 6 : Strategy Parameter Tuning Panel
The Strategy Parameter Tuning Panel transforms Dynamic Portfolio Rebalancing using Reinforcement Learning from a fixed model into an interactive simulation workbench.

Users can adjust key financial and RL parameters through intuitive sliders and dropdowns, then immediately re-run the strategy to observe how changes affect portfolio performance - all without touching any code.
This makes the platform valuable as both an educational tool and a practical research environment.
Key Features:
•  Risk Aversion slider (γ: 1-10) controls the Merton model’s conservatism; lower γ produces higher equity allocation, higher γ shifts weight toward cash.
•  Transaction Cost Rate slider (0.0% - 0.5%) adjusts the per-rebalance cost applied to both strategies, enabling sensitivity analysis on turnover efficiency.
•  Risk-Free Rate (rf) dropdown (5% - 8% p.a.) updates the Sharpe ratio baseline and Merton weight formula, reflecting different prevailing interest rate environments.
•  Dual Execution Modes: Autonomous PPO (full auto-pilot - agent rebalances without asking) and Advisory Mode (AI recommends weights - user reviews and approves before execution).
⚙ Tech Stack:  Streamlit (sliders + dropdowns)  |  PPO re-inference (Stable-Baselines3)  |  Plotly (live chart update)
Example Workflow
Scenario: An investor logs into Dynamic Portfolio Rebalancing using Reinforcement Learning on a high-volatility day (NIFTY -2.1%, NASDAQ -1.8%).
•  Step 1: Interactive Web Dashboard
The investor opens the dashboard. The Volatility Regime Badge flashes "⚠ HIGH STRESS".
The NASDAQ drawdown chart shows - 8.3% from the 60-day peak. EMA 20 is below EMA 60 - bearish signal.
•  Step 2: User Login & Authentication
The investor logs in. bcrypt verifies the hashed password; a signed JWT is issued.
Server routes the investor to their Portfolio Tracker workspace. Current NAV: ₹3,12,500 (PPO Agent active).
•  Step 3: Live Market Data Integration
yfinance pulls latest NIFTY (^NSEI) and NASDAQ-100 (^NDX) daily closing prices.
All 13 state features are computed in-memory. The RL state vector is assembled and passed to PPO.
Example Workflow
•  Step 4: RL Working Process
PPO agent receives the 13-feature state (high vol regime, negative rolling Sharpe).
Softmax output: NASDAQ 15%  |  NIFTY 10%  |  Cash 75%  - heavy cash for capital preservation.
•  Step 5: Portfolio Tracker
NAV updates to ₹3,09,875 (−0.84%). Donut chart redraws: 75% Cash, 15% NASDAQ, 10% NIFTY.
Daily P&L: −₹2,625. RL agent preserved ₹3,625 vs. an equal-weight all-equity portfolio.
•  Step 6: Strategy Parameter Tuning Panel
Investor slides γ: 5 → 2 (Aggressive). PPO re-infers: NASDAQ 40%, NIFTY 25%, Cash 35%.
Advisory Mode popup: 'AI recommends rebalancing - Approve or Dismiss?' Investor approves.
Example Workflow
Outcome & System Value
❖Portfolio is rebalanced instantly with 0.1% transaction cost deducted. The trade is logged with timestamp, weights applied, and cost incurred.
❖Merton model (γ=5) allocates NASDAQ 28%, NIFTY 22%, Cash 50% - less defensive than RL. RL’s cash-heavy posture yields a 37% lower drawdown than Merton on this crisis day.
❖End-of-day: RL NAV ₹3,09,875  vs  Merton NAV ₹3,07,100 - RL outperforms by ₹2,775 through superior regime detection.
